claim.content: For adsorption of first-row and transition-metal atoms on ionic oxide surfaces within density-functional theory, the Local Density Approximation (LDA) tends to give adsorption energies that are systematically larger (i.e. predict stronger binding) than those obtained with standard gradient-corrected functionals such as the Perdew–Wang Generalized Gradient Approximation (GGA); numerically in the Cu/MgO calculations reported here this manifests as an LDA monomer adsorption energy E_{S-A} ≈ 1.46 eV compared with the GGA ≈ 0.99 eV value, indicating that the LDA overbinds relative to GGA for this system.
